ai.description: The Gansi Caecilian reaches 20–25 cm. It is dark brown dorsally with a paler venter. Distinctive features include a rounded snout, 115–125 primary annuli, and a lack of secondary grooves.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus gansi* is best distinguished by its lack of secondary annuli on the posterior third of the body, a feature that sets it apart from all other Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Uraeotyphlus gansi* inhabits moist, leaf-littered soil within tropical evergreen forests and cardamom plantations in the Western Ghats at altitudes of 600–1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: The Gansi Caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uraeotyphlus gansi* is oviparous, laying small clutches of terrestrial eggs in underground nests. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus gansi* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in the Indian state of Kerala, typically inhabiting mid-to-high elevations in moist forest regions.
ai.callDescription: The Gansi Caecilian is a limbless amphibian and does not produce an advertisement call, as caecilians lack vocal cords and rely on tactile and chemical cues.
